subject: Exec slate approval + EB prep checklist for Acme close
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exec slate approval + EB prep checklist for Acme close

Team —

We’re at the stage where the MAP and the EB (executive briefing) agenda need sign-off so we can lock the boardroom slot with Acme next week. High-level ask: review the attached MAP_v2.xlsx and EB_prep_checklist.docx and confirm the exec slate + asks by EOD Wednesday (12/22).

Quick context: Acme wants a senior exec briefing the week of 12/28 to finalize procurement and legal gating items. Our mutual action plan is updated to reflect a two-step EB: 1) product value + integration runway with the CTO/VP Eng; 2) executive sponsor alignment with CEO/Head of Product to commit to capacity and terms.

Proposed exec slate (please flag edits):
- CTO: Ana Torres (Acme) — technical adoption + pilot sizing
- CEO/Head of Product: TBD (we should ask for CEO if possible; Laura can advise)
- Procurement: Acme procurement lead (cc’ed in follow-up)

Key dependencies for EB to close:
- Confirm sponsor (Ana vs. CEO) and who will champion the internal economic case
- Legal redline window (Acme legal to return by 12/27)
- PO path / procurement steps (procurement contact + earliest PO date)

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (17KB)], [Attachment: EB_prep_checklist.docx (12KB)]

Next steps:
- Marissa: sponsor outreach and runbook for the EB agenda
- Karthik: finalize the demo slate + latency/cost slides for the CTO call
- Laura: advise on exec ask wording and whether CEO slot is realistic
- Rachel: prep CS handoff and post-EB adoption play

If we confirm today, I’ll send an invite with the two-part EB agenda and the invite list.

Thanks —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Ana Torres <ana@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exec slate approval + EB prep checklist for Acme close

Rishi —

Thanks, this is actionable. A few quick points:

1) Ana’s the right CTO contact; she’s asked internally for a short CTO-level session. I’ll own the outreach to secure her slot.

2) CEO is preferable for the final sponsor ask but might be a stretch the week of 12/28. Suggest offering two windows: 12/29 AM PST or 1/4 AM PST as fallback.

3) I’ve updated the MAP with a column for "sponsor owner" and added estimated legal turnaround (see MAP_v2, column G).

4) We should lock the EB agenda to 45 minutes for execs, with a separate 60-minute technical deep-dive for the CTO/engineering stakeholders. Karthik, can you rework the demo to a 20-minute highlight + Q&A?

I’ll start sponsor outreach to Ana and cc procurement if it looks like legal will need clarification on the data residency clause.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Exec slate approval + EB prep checklist for Acme close

Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for the clear summary. I can do a CTO-level session on 12/29 AM PST (preferred) or 1/4 AM PST (backup). For the exec sponsor slot: I will advocate for a Head of Product presence but cannot promise CEO attendance; our CEO is traveling that week. If you craft the ask as a single decision — capacity + PO path — that will increase the chance we get a VP-level sponsor to commit.

A few asks from our side:
- Can you include the pilot success metric targets (uptime SLA, latency p50/p95 targets) in the EB slides?
- Legal: please confirm we have a short note on data residency and retention (one slide).
- Procurement: I’ve looped Procurement and Dave Li for scheduling and PO expectations. Procurement has internal blackout 12/24–12/27, so they’ll only action after 12/28.

Forwarding the MAP_v2 to Dave for procurement visibility.

Best,
Ana Torres
CTO, Acme Corp

Rishi / team —

Thanks for pulling this together. A couple of small edits to the EB prep checklist:
- Slide for pilot KPIs: separate into business metrics (NRR/usage) and SRE targets (p50/p95).
- Sponsor ask language: replace "capacity and terms" with "capacity commitment and procurement path" — more explicit for execs.
- Add a one-line "risks & mitigations" slide so the sponsor can see blockers up-front.

I’ll add suggested language in the EB_prep_checklist document and push a change to the MAP (column H) with the sponsor-ask wording.

Laura
VP, Strategic Accounts
